text:
Maya (CS): Escalating a report from LedgerPro (prod). After the rollout of rwd-3.3-compact some daily summary outputs are including vendors that do not exist in the customer's ledger. They provided a minimal repro and a CSV of transactions. They say this was not happening on rwd-3.2-stable.
Oliver: Please paste the exact request and any org id/timestamps.
Maya (CS): Org: ledgerpro-prod. Timestamp: 2026-03-12T15:22:18Z. Repro request (sanitized):
```
POST /v1/chat/completions
{
  "model": "rwd-3.3-compact",
  "messages": [
    {"role":"system","content":"You are an assistant that summarizes daily accounting transactions into vendor-level line items using ONLY facts from the input. Do NOT invent vendors, invoice numbers, or amounts."},
    {"role":"user","content":"Input: Transactions:\n- 2026-03-11 Wire to acct ****1234 ref SAL-INV 421.\n- 2026-03-11 ACH to acct ****9876 invoice 9871."}
  ],
  "temperature": 0.0
}
```
Maya (CS): Customer's returned summary (redacted) included a line: "Vendor: Greenwick Trading â€” Total: $2,340.00 â€” Invoices: GT-421". Their raw CSV contains Acme Office Supplies and two bank transfers; no Greenwick.
Emma (Research): Temperature 0.0 reduces sampling noise. Any recent model-side changes to tokenization or system-message handling?
Li (Eng): 3.3-compact introduced a tokenizer remap (saves mem) and we adjusted assistant/system concat order slightly for streaming. Could be related.
Oliver: Can we get the verbatim model output from the customer?
Maya (CS): Yes, verbatim snippet below:
```
Vendor: Greenwick Trading â€” Total: $2,340.00 â€” Invoices: GT-421
Vendor: Acme Office Supplies â€” Total: $120.00 â€” Invoice: 9871
```
Maya (CS): They repeated that another test produced a fabricated bank-fee line item. They're worried this will break reconciliations.
Li (Eng): If the system prompt concatenation order changed we might be truncating or re-ordering the explicit safety sentence. Token remap could also make certain invoice prefixes map to tokens that trigger memorized vendor names.
Emma (Research): Ask the customer to allow us to pin their traffic to 3.2 while we investigate. Also we need token-level logprobs and kv-cache traces; if they can't share full logs we need permission to run identical inputs against canary binaries.
Maya (CS): LedgerPro agreed to pinning and to run private tests but can't share logs. They've given permission to route their traffic away from the canary.
deploy-bot: rollout/rwd-3.3-compact canary: 12% traffic since 2026-03-11T00:00:00Z. AFFECTED_ORGS: ledgerpro-prod present in canary pool. (details: https://deploys.internal/rollouts/3821)
Li (Eng): Applying per-org routing override: ledgerpro-prod -> rwd-3.2-stable. ETA ~30s. Also adding a temporary response filter: for high-sensitivity customers, if generated vendor tokens are not present in the input and model confidence < 0.60, suppress and return a clarification note.
deploy-bot: routing change applied: ledgerpro-prod -> rwd-3.2-stable (took 18s).
Maya (CS): Customer confirmed traffic now hitting rwd-3.2-stable and their quick checks look normal. They want notification before future model switches and weekly updates until fixed.
Li (Eng): Reproducing locally with canary binary now. Repro command:
```
python tests/repro_chat.py \n  --model rwd-3.3-compact \n  --system "You are an assistant that summarizes..." \n  --user "Input: Transactions: ..." \n  --temperature 0.0 \n  --logprobs 5 \n  --save-kv /tmp/kv-debug.json
```
Li (Eng): Early result: I can reproduce a Greenwick vendor hallucination locally against the canary binary. Next-token logprobs show a moderate spike initiating the vendor token sequence; attaching traces to ISSUE-5821.
Emma (Research): If reproducible that's very helpful. Hypotheses: 1) tokenizer remap changed token boundaries creating token sequences that match memorized vendor names; 2) assistant/system concat reorder reduced the weight of the explicit "Do NOT invent vendors" instruction; 3) cache or retrieval contamination from unrelated contexts. We'll run a differential eval on an anonymized ledger prompt set (target: 200 examples).
Oliver: Also check if any retrieval or short-term context caching layer was engaged for the canary only. If unrelated cached contexts were used, they could leak vendor names.
Jess (Product): This is P1 for customers with financial workloads. Proposed immediate plan: (A) Per-customer pinning (done), (B) hold 3.3 canary for finance tenants and roll back canary for affected groups, (C) root-cause analysis + fix, (D) expand regression tests to include ledger prompt set, (E) customer-facing postmortem. Approve? :thumbsup:
Oliver: Approve. Also create an internal quick-check that flags vendor tokens in outputs not present in input for finance-sensitive orgs.
Li (Eng): I'll try a hotfix to restore previous system concat order and run the regression suite. If that solves, we'll cut rwd-3.3.1 with the concat fix. If not, fallback is to revert tokenizer remap and re-run. Working on a PR.
Maya (CS): Created tracker ticket: https://tracker.internal/ISSUE-5821 (P1 â€” hallucinated vendors after rwd-3.3 canary). Pasting into external support ticket and notifying LedgerPro.
Emma (Research): I'll run the differential eval harness overnight and post a report with tokenizer diffs, logprob heatmaps, and recommended mitigations by 2026-03-13 08:00 UTC.
Li (Eng): Quick note: kv-cache dumps show no obvious cross-request contamination for these repros, leaning towards tokenizer/concat as top suspects. Attaching KV traces to the ticket when cleansed.
Maya (CS): Customer asked for ETA on root cause and a timeline for fix. We committed to every-4-hour updates and the customer is OK with that cadence.
Jess (Product): If this is tokenizer-related we should consider a staged rollout policy for any tokenizer/serialization changes, especially for tenants with regulatory/financial sensitivity. :rotating_light:
Oliver: Follow-ups assigned: Li (root cause & PR), Emma (eval + diffs), Maya (customer comms), Jess (postmortem + external comms). Update this thread with ticket/PR links.
Maya (CS): LedgerPro responded: "Thanks for the rapid response. This hits month-end reconciliations so please prioritize. Keep us posted." End of thread for now; will update when we have PR or deep-dive artifacts.
